How can I create AI product photos from a reference image with tested prompts and visible inputs and outputs? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
Creating AI product photos from a reference image requires a structured workflow to maintain product fidelity while placing the item in realistic scenes. Platforms like Tolstoy and Nightjar recommend a source-guided approach where a real photo provides the exact geometry, while AI generates the background and lighting. 
nightjar.so
 +1
Here is how you can set up a visible workflow with tested prompt frameworks, inputs, and outputs.
Step 1: Define the Visible Inputs
Before prompting, you must isolate the product identity from the scene. Do not rely on AI to invent your product from scratch. 
www.gotolstoy.com
 +2
The Product Reference Image: A clean, high-resolution photo of the actual product, ideally taken against a plain or transparent background. 
nightjar.so
 +1
The Visual Style Reference (Optional): A separate inspirational photo that establishes the exact lighting, angle, or mood you want to emulate. 
PrompTessor
Step 2: Use a Tested Prompt Formula
Effective product photography prompts must tightly control art direction while instructing the AI on what not to change. Experts at PrompTessor suggest using a highly structured, bounded format to prevent the AI from altering brand logos or textures: 
PrompTessor
The Blueprint Formula:
[Placement/Channel] of [Product Description] placed on [Surface Details] in a [Scene Environment]. [Camera Angle] view, [Lighting Style], [Depth of Field]. Keep the product shape, logo, and texture identical to the reference image.
🏷️ Tested Prompt Templates
Studio Catalog Listing (Clean & Professional):
"Ecommerce marketplace listing image of the product from the reference photo. The item is centered on a seamless, crisp white background with a subtle, soft drop shadow beneath it. Front-facing eye-level view, bright diffused studio lighting, ultra-sharp focus. Maintain exact product colors and label details."
 
www.gotolstoy.com
 +1
Outdoor Lifestyle Scene (Social Media & Ads):
"Commercial advertising creative featuring the product from the reference photo. The item is resting on a wet, dark volcanic rock. In the background, a misty Pacific Northwest forest is heavily blurred. Close-up macro shot, dramatic morning golden hour sunlight with realistic lens flare, shallow depth of field. Do not alter the product packaging."
 
PrompTessor
Minimalist Interior Scene (Home & Decor):
"Lifestyle mockup of the product from the reference photo. The product is placed on a light beige travertine stone block next to a small, delicate ceramic vase with a single dried pampas grass stem. Minimalist Japandi concrete bathroom background. High-angle shot, soft morning window light creating gentle shadows, photorealistic texture."
 
nightjar.so
 +1
Step 3: Connect Inputs to Outputs via AI Platforms
To see your inputs and outputs clearly side-by-side, utilize generation tools that support explicit image-to-image or canvas workflows: 
EaseMate AI
 +1
Upload the Reference: In tools like Leonardo.Ai or Picsart, upload your product photo into the "Image Guidance" or "Image-to-Image" slot.
Apply Advanced Node Workflows: For a highly visual and scalable pipeline, platform tutorials like those for Runway AI demonstrate using visual canvas nodes. You can hook an LLM node (like Claude) directly to your product photo input to automatically generate contextual scene prompts, making the entire chain of inputs, prompts, and outputs fully visible.
Lock the Product: Use features like "Product Inpainting" or "Canvas Inpainting" to erase the original background while locking the product pixels in place, ensuring the AI only alters the surroundings. 
YouTube
·Learn How To Edit Stuff
 +4
Step 4: Evaluate the Outputs (The Fidelity Gate)
AI can accidentally warp text, logos, or proportions. Establish a strict quality assurance review by comparing the output directly against your reference image using these checkmarks: 
nightjar.so
 +1
Product Fidelity: Are the brand logos, labels, and text sharp and readable?
Lighting Integration: Does the light bouncing off the generated background naturally match the highlights on the product?
Shadow Realism: Is there a realistic contact shadow where the product touches the generated surface, or does it look like it's "floating"? 
Leonardo.Ai
 +3
If a specific detail (like a bottle cap or clasp) fails twice, adjust your prompt to add stricter exclusions or refine the input packet. Once a prompt formula passes, save it as a repeatable "Recipe" to scale across other variants or SKUs in your catalog. 
nightjar.so
 +2
To help tailor a specific prompt or setup for you, tell me:
What type of product are you photographing? (e.g., cosmetics, shoes, electronics)
What kind of aesthetic or background do you want to create?
Which AI generation tool are you currently using or planning to use?
